memory_update.text: HSTM should be carried forward as the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for the healthcare-licensure / hybrid-campus capacity node because it directly overlaps clinical education, credentialing, simulation-based education, and clinical-rotation management.

CAE should be carried forward as a simulation-equipment / healthcare-training supplier, but later layers must test segment materiality because healthcare simulation may be small relative to aviation and defense.
PSO should be carried forward as a regulated testing-infrastructure candidate through Pearson VUE / NCLEX, with materiality and contract economics as the primary evidence gaps.

LOPE is useful as a reference demand and capacity anchor, not as the main underfollowed supplier; its disclosures support the thesis that hybrid healthcare education may be constrained by licensure, clinical placements, simulation labs, and campus utilization.

Several important clinical-placement and healthcare-education suppliers appear private or not clearly US-listed, including InPlace Software, CAUHEC Connect, CORE Higher Ed, Precepta, UWorld, Laerdal, and Ascend Learning; later passes should track whether any public parent, IPO path, or listed distributor exists.

node: Healthcare licensure and hybrid campus capacity
summary: Expanded the healthcare-licensure / hybrid-campus capacity node toward scarce suppliers and regulated infrastructure rather than generic online education. The strongest underfollowed public-market exposure found in this pass is HealthStream, because it touches clinical education, credentialing, simulation-based education, and clinical-rotation management. CAE is a simulation-equipment and healthcare-training infrastructure supplier, but healthcare is likely a smaller segment inside a larger aviation/defense simulation business. Pearson is a regulated testing infrastructure anchor through Pearson VUE / NCLEX, with less pure exposure but high chokepoint relevance. Grand Canyon Education is included only as a reference capacity operator because its disclosures directly mention ABSN/OTA hybrid growth, simulation technology, virtual reality, state licensure needs, and employer pipelines.
